one_ray_full_fan_theorems.uniform_statement: For z^2=yz=0, g is at most the sum over k from n-ell to min(m,n-1) of 1+4*(n-k)*ceil(log2(n-k)), hence O(n^2 log(n+1)). For xz=yz=0 the overlap is at most one, giving the sharp worst order Theta(n log(n+1)), with characteristic-zero lower examples.
one_ray_full_fan_theorems.sharp_quadratic_fixture: K[t]/t^(2m), x=t, y=t^m(1+t)^m, z=t^m(1+t)^(2m). In characteristic zero or p>3m-1, the full fan has binomial(m+2,2) cones, a triangular lattice adjacency graph, and W=L=m(m+1)(m+2)+sum_(i+j<=m-1)|i-j|. At m=p^s in characteristic p it has exactly three cones.
one_ray_full_fan_theorems.scope: Ordinary contraction and the saved planar matroid bound are established inputs. The contraction is not an algebra quotient. Exact priority is unassessed; the logarithm for the square-zero-ray class and the general two-planar-branch problem remain unresolved.

uniform_common_factor_pencil_theorem: For every field and every length-n I containing l0*l1,l0*l2 for nonconstant affine linear l0 and affine linear l1,l2 with independent linear parts, g(I)<=6*sum_(j=1)^n (1+4*j*ceil(log2(j)))=O(n^2 log(n+1)). This uses actual original-coordinate matroids on at most six initial carriers; no fan invariance under a linear change is assumed.

exact_fixtures.sharp_family: H_r=(x^(r+1),yz,y(x,y)^r,z(x,z)^r), quotient by x^i(y^(r-i)-z^(r-i)) for 0<=i<r and x^r-y^r.
exact_fixtures.axis_padding: Direct product with K[x]/((x-1)^t), y=z=0; t=1 or 2r+1.

primary_sources.scope: Sections 1--2, equations (1.0.2), (1.1.3), (2.0.1), (2.1.3) and Theorem 2.8: classical fiber products, diagonal module quotients and additional Gorenstein hypotheses. No new gluing operation or exact-priority conclusion.

Introduction Theorem 1 and Theorem 4.6: graded connected sums require a common contraction of dual generators and an equality of annihilator ideals; no arbitrary nonhomogeneous fan-counting assertion follows.
Introduction and Theorem 4.3 concern connected sums over the residue field, rather than arbitrary shared-K[x] couplings. No exact quantitative-priority conclusion.

limits: Finite checks support implementations; all-field and all-length results rely on the self-contained proof.

The invariant-factor theorem, planar staircase estimate, fiber products, socle criterion and module quotients are established. Exact priority of the combined sharp resource inequalities is unassessed.
Module generator count is not vector-space dimension. The polynomial x-action and original monomial labels must be retained.
The sharp large-generator family has only three or four cones; it is not a large-fan witness.
The one-ray counts require z^2=yz=0 or xz=yz=0. They do not bound every yz=0 coupling. Their classical matroid ingredients and exact priority are distinguished in the proof.

The Pascal-ray example has a quadratic fan in characteristic zero and a constant fan at characteristic-p prime-power lengths. The square-zero-ray upper bound still has an unresolved logarithmic factor.

The common-factor pencil theorem covers arbitrary linear forms, but not a general pair of quadrics without a common linear factor. The two-quadratic-monomial corollary requires actual relations, not merely heads in one initial ideal.
No full yz=0 fan bound, unrestricted G3 improvement, supergeneric lower separation or completed goal follows.
